reforms.description: The Canada Millennium Scholarships programme was created to address accessibility and affordability issues in post-secondary education, providing 100,000 scholarships per year starting in 2000, targeted based on needs and merit. Additionally, the Youth Internship Canada initiative was announced, providing funds for internships aimed at unemployed and underemployed youth to gain experience in growth areas of the economy.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These initiatives aim to enhance the skills and employability of youth, thereby supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Both initiatives have been successfully implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Both initiatives represent significant reforms aimed at improving human capital in Canada.
reforms.source_quote: The 1998 federal budget attempts to address the issues of accessibility and affordability of post-secondary education through the creation of the Canada Millennium Scholarships programme.

reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced the Employment Insurance (EI) system, which includes active employment benefits aimed at providing training and assistance to individuals re-entering the labor market.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The EI system supports workforce reintegration, enhancing human capital and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The EI system has been fully implemented and operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of the EI system represents a major reform in employment support.
reforms.source_quote: The new Employment Insurance (EI) system includes both a component focused on delivering benefits and one concentrated on delivering training and other assistance to speed up re-integration into the labour market.

reforms.description: Saskatchewan announced a new corporate tax credit for research and development, aimed at incentivizing private sector investment in R&D activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The tax credit is designed to stimulate private sector investment in R&D, fostering innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The tax credit has been successfully implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, the tax credit is a narrower reform compared to broader initiatives.
reforms.source_quote: Saskatchewan announced a new corporate tax credit for research and development.

reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established with an initial funding of C$ 800 million to enhance research infrastructure and support innovation in Canadian universities and research institutions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research infrastructure is critical for advancing scientific research and innovation capabilities.
reforms.status_evidence: The foundation has been fully operational since its establishment.
reforms.importance_rationale: The establishment of the Canada Foundation for Innovation represents a major reform in research infrastructure funding.
reforms.source_quote: the Canada Foundation for Innovation with up-front funding of C$ 800 million

reforms.description: The Ontario government announced a C$ 500 million fund dedicated to research and development, aimed at fostering innovation and supporting job creation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The fund is intended to stimulate R&D activities, which can lead to job creation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The fund has been successfully implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The fund represents a significant but narrower initiative compared to broader reforms.
reforms.source_quote: Other highlights include increased spending for health care and job creation; C$ 500 million for a ten-year research and development fund; and tax credits for small businesses.
